extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers and authors (novelists, short-story writers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for choosing and writing setting descriptions that immerse readers—covering scene selection, POV-driven detail, sensory work, avoiding clichés, and economical prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose strong scene settings / Ensure settings have purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Select settings deliberately; every setting should do more than serve as a backdrop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settings can: set a mood; give depth and context to a story-world; amplify the conflict or tension in a scene; reveal elements of characterization; deepen the story’s themes. When choosing or strengthening scene settings, consider what is happening in the scene and which character will serve as the point-of-view. Ask how you can manipulate the setting to set the tone you want readers to experience while fulfilling the needs of the scene’s events and amplifying the emotions your POV character will undergo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Get inside your character’s head (use Deep POV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Write setting descriptions that reflect the POV character’s worldview, experiences, and personality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you’re writing in Deep POV (the reader experiences events through the POV character’s eyes), craft descriptions to show how that specific character would perceive and engage with their surroundings—not neutral, omniscient description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilize sensory details
rubrics_metrics.description: Include sensory input (touch, taste, sound, sight, smell) to make settings vivid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With your POV character in mind, include key sensory details that matter for the moment. You don’t need to include every sense in every scene, but touching on the most impactful senses at a given moment helps breathe life into the pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with the setting (avoid info-dumps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate description into action and perception rather than dumping it in a single paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Info-dumps pull readers out of the narrative. Describe how the POV character physically reacts or interacts with the environment (e.g., 'their nose wrinkles as the sharp smell of vinegar fills the air' or 'their body sighs into the warm embrace of their bed'). Sprinkle descriptive elements throughout the scene to create touchstones that keep readers immersed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose impactful details
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on details that serve one or more scene purposes (mood, context, conflict, characterization, theme).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider what you are trying to accomplish in the scene, then describe elements that help achieve those ends. Example: in a sword-fight, emphasize details that amplify tension (skittering loose stones underfoot, the whiz of a blade) rather than unrelated ornamentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid clichés
rubrics_metrics.description: Steer clear of overused phrases and conventional setting-tropes or put a fresh spin on them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize clichéd pairings (e.g., funeral + rainy day) and either avoid them or subvert them by finding original sensory or symbolic angles (e.g., oppressive humidity representing the overbearing shadow of death vs. driving wind symbolizing chaotic grief).

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor brevity and power
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer concise, strong wording over flowery, adjective-heavy prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Err on the side of brevity—choose strong, simple words that evoke tone. Anti-pattern: overly elaborate, vague sentences that conflict in tone. Example of weak: 'The soft warm amber glow of the candlelight shimmered through the room, sending rapid, tantalizing chills down her spine.' Example of stronger: 'Warm candlelight filled the room, whispering of promise, alighting her senses.' The stronger version removes unnecessary adjectives and clarifies purpose/tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Think like a filmmaker
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame and craft scenes visually to bring settings to life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because modern fiction often uses a more visual style and Deep POV, consider cinematic framing and visual composition when deciding what to show and how to describe it. (The article links to a more detailed guide on writing description with filmmaking in mind.)
